en_alt: The first-aid kit has run out of bandage.
note: Adds the equally natural rendering with the kit as subject.

en_alt: They covered the wound with clean bandages.
note: The Russian is an impersonal plural, so the active reading is equally valid.

en_alt: The battle went on all day.
note: Alternative rendering of продолжалась that keeps the word-bank drill fair.

ru: Об э́той би́тве пи́шут в кни́гах.
en_alt: They write about this battle in books.
note: Impersonal plural: the active reading is as good as the passive one.

ru: Он де́лал всё для бла́га семьи́.

en_alt: All the benefits belong to the people.
note: Plural блага reads as benefits/good things as readily as 'goods', which in English suggests merchandise.

en_alt: The glare of the sun blinded me.
note: Glare is the natural English for блеск солнца; en_gb keeps the headword gloss.

en_alt: A gleam appeared in her eyes.
note: English idiom prefers 'a gleam' for a shine in the eyes; en_gb keeps the gloss word.

en: The teacher is pleased with the twins.
en_alt: The teacher is glad about the twins.
note: рада близнецам says she is glad of them, not that she has them; 'to have' is invented.

en_alt: She keeps a blog about travel.
note: 'keeps' is an equally standard rendering of ведёт here.

en_alt: The blog already has a lot of readers.
note: много renders as 'a lot of' as readily as 'many'.

ru: Две страны́ вступи́ли в вое́нный блок.

en_alt: The house is built of concrete blocks.
note: 'built of' is the commoner English collocation and equally literal.

en_alt: There are a lot of blouses hanging in the cupboard.
note: шкаф is glossed 'cupboard' corpus-wide; adds that reading without changing en_gb.

en_alt: She arrived in a new blouse.
note: 'arrived' is the more idiomatic English for пришла here.

en_alt: There were various dishes on the table.
note: English normally uses 'there were' where Russian uses стояли.

en_alt: The country is proud of its wealth.
note: Adds the headword gloss reading alongside 'riches'.

ru: В э́том бою́ поги́бло мно́го люде́й.
Солда́ты вступи́ли в бой на рассве́те.
Он лежа́л на боку́ и чита́л.
Ло́шадь повора́чивалась то одни́м бо́ком, то други́м.
en_alt: The horse kept turning first one side, then the other.
note: 'first … then' is the more usual English for то … то, and the imperfective is iterative.

en_alt: The fans are shouting at the stadium.
note: на стадионе maps equally to 'at the stadium'.

en_alt: The team thanked their fans.
note: British usage takes a plural pronoun for a team as readily as 'its'.

en_alt: Tighten the bolt with a nut.
note: закрутить is 'tighten/screw up' as much as 'fasten'.

ru: В кла́ссе всегда́ есть па́ра болтуно́в.
en: There are always a couple of chatterboxes in the class.
en_alt: There is always a pair of chatterboxes in the class.
note: пара here means 'a couple of', not a matched pair; 'a pair of chatterboxes' is not idiomatic English.

ru: От бо́ли он не мог спать.
en_alt: He could not sleep because of the pain.
note: 'because of' is the commoner English for causal от.

en_alt: He feels severe pain.
note: English usually has 'severe pain' without an article; en_gb stays literal.

ru: В городски́х больни́цах не хвата́ет враче́й.
en_alt: There are not enough doctors in the city hospitals.
note: не хватает renders as 'not enough' as naturally as 'short of'.

en_alt: They are building a hospital next to the house.
note: рядом с is literally 'next to'.

en_alt: He was taken to hospital.
note: Impersonal plural: the passive is equally valid British English.

en_alt: He is in the hospital.
note: Accepts the article-bearing variant alongside the British bare form.

en_alt: Most students like the course.
note: 'Most students' is the commoner English for большинству студентов.

en_alt: Without his beard you would not recognise him.
note: The impersonal infinitive construction reads naturally with 'you' too.

en_alt: The captain stood on board the ship.
note: 'on board' tracks на борту more closely than 'aboard'.

ru: Он посвяти́л жизнь борьбе́ с боле́знями.
en_alt: He devoted his life to the fight against illness.
note: болезнями is glossed 'illness'; adds the commoner English collocation.

ru: В суббо́ту мы идём на бо́улинг.
О́пытный бо́цман знал ка́ждый у́зел на корабле́.

en_alt: The boatswain ordered the sailors to tidy the deck.
note: убрать is 'tidy/clear up' as much as 'clean'.

ru: Брази́лия — са́мая больша́я страна́ Ю́жной Аме́рики.
en_alt: Brazil is the biggest country in South America.
note: самая большая is literally 'the biggest'.

ru: Они́ прожи́ли в бра́ке два́дцать лет.
en: They were married for twenty years.
en_alt: They spent twenty years in marriage.
note: 'lived in marriage' is translationese; English says 'were married for' or 'spent … in marriage'.

ru: Я е́ду в го́сти к бра́тьям.

en_alt: I gave my brother a watch as a present.
note: подарил is specifically 'gave as a present'; the plain 'gave' stays as en_gb.

en: You are stopping your brother from working.
en_alt: You are disturbing your brother's work.
note: мешать + infinitive is 'stop/hinder from doing'; 'while he works' invents a temporal clause the Russian does not have.

ru: Мой брат живёт в друго́м го́роде.

en_alt: The parents bought identical bicycles for the brothers.
note: The dative can surface as a for-phrase; both orders are correct English.

en: She took offence at her brother.
en_alt: She took offence at my brother.
note: With a third-person subject and no possessive, the default reading of на брата is the subject's own brother, not the speaker's.

en_alt: Big logs are floating on the river.
note: большие is glossed 'big'; the progressive matches the imperfective плывут.

ru: Он сел на бревно́ у костра́.

en_alt: The workers carried heavy logs.
note: The past imperfective carries both the simple past and the progressive in English.

en_alt: The foreman handed out the tasks to the workers.
note: раздал is literally 'handed out'.

ru: Я поговори́ла с бригади́ром о пла́не.

note: The singular eyebrow is odd but the Russian and English agree, and the singular is what the declension slot needs.

en_alt: She knitted her brows.
note: 'furrowed her eyebrows' is slightly off; 'knitted her brows' is the idiomatic English.

en_alt: I was talking with a Buddhist.
note: разговаривала is imperfective, so the progressive past is equally right.

ru: Ря́дом с до́мом откры́ли но́вую бу́лочную.
en_alt: They have opened a new bakery next to the house.
note: Impersonal plural открыли: the active reading is equally valid.

en_alt: I bought bread in the bakery.
note: в булочной is literally 'in the bakery'.

en_alt: She threw out the old bits of paper.
note: выбросила is literally 'threw out'; бумажки are bits/scraps of paper.

en_alt: There is a small piece of paper on the table.
note: English normally uses 'there is' where Russian uses лежит.

en_alt: There are only two rooms in the bungalow.
note: The locative construction reads naturally as a 'there are' sentence.

ru: Они́ сня́ли бунга́ло на берегу́ мо́ря.
en_alt: They rented a bungalow on the seashore.
note: на берегу моря is literally 'on the shore of the sea'.

ru: На за́втрак он съел бутербро́д с сы́ром.
en_alt: For breakfast he ate a sandwich with cheese.
note: Keeps the с сыром prepositional phrase visible for the word-bank drill.

en_alt: We need to stay within the budget.
note: 'stay within' is the commoner English collocation; надо is impersonal, so 'we' is a reasonable default on both.

ru: В на́шем бюдже́те нет ли́шних де́нег.

en_alt: The government passed a new budget.
note: приняло бюджет is 'passed' as readily as 'adopted'.

ru: Без вай-фа́й я как без рук.
en_alt: Without Wi-Fi I am helpless.
note: как без рук is an idiom ('as if without hands'); the added alt gives the plain reading while en_gb stays idiomatic.

en_alt: An enormous boulder lay on the shore.
note: огромный is glossed 'enormous'.

en_alt: The exchange rate changes every day.
note: курс валюты is idiomatically 'the exchange rate'.

ru: Он храни́т де́ньги в иностра́нной валю́те.

en_alt: She is taking a hot bath.
note: Adds the uncontracted form so the word-bank drill accepts it.

en_alt: There is a lot of water in the bath.
note: Adds the uncontracted form so the word-bank drill accepts it.

ru: Мы покра́сили ва́нную в бе́лый цвет.

en_alt: The bathroom is located on the right.
note: находится is literally 'is located'.

en_alt: She took a shower in the bathroom.
note: 'took a shower' is as standard as 'had a shower'.

en_alt: This mitten has no match.
note: 'has no pair' is understandable but 'no match' is the idiomatic English.

en_alt: There are several possible solutions.
note: варианты решения is idiomatically 'possible solutions'; en_gb keeps the headword gloss.

en_alt: We agreed to this option.
note: вариант is commonly 'option' in this sense.

en_alt: People used to tell of two witches.
note: The past imperfective рассказывали carries the habitual reading too.
